name: Arelate supply aqueduct
summary: A spring-fed Roman aqueduct branch that carried water to the city of Arelate (Arles) before part of its flow was diverted to the Barbegal mills.
description: Southern spring-fed aqueduct branch supplying Arelate before diversion to Barbegal.
tier_reason: A particular supply branch is useful fine detail; its place in Barbegal does not establish a separate broad advance. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

date.label: 50–120 CE
date.basis: The 2018 site account states this interval of city-supply use; original construction is not independently dated.

events.statement: Southern spring-fed aqueduct branch supplying Arelate before diversion to Barbegal.
events.caveats: Chronology is inherited archaeological synthesis; the branch is not the whole Arelate water system.

evidence.supports: City-supply interval and identity of the southern branch.
First-century city-supply branches and later detachment of the southern branch.
